passages.text: On a hot afternoon a street lined with trees can be eight degrees cooler than a street of the same width without them. Part of the difference is shade, but not all of it: a tree also pumps water from the soil into the air through its leaves, and evaporation takes heat with it. City councils have begun to treat trees as a piece of equipment rather than as decoration, and some now count the cooling they provide in the same accounts as air conditioning. The catch is that a young tree does very little. A newly planted sapling gives almost no shade, and it may be twenty years before it earns its place. Cities that cut down old trees and plant twice as many small ones therefore grow hotter first.

Snow that falls on Antarctica never melts. It is buried by the snow of the following year and pressed into ice, and the tiny bubbles trapped inside it keep a sample of the air from the day it fell. Drilling teams pull out cylinders of this ice, some of them from three kilometres down, and read the layers as one reads the rings of a tree. The deepest ice recovered so far is about eight hundred thousand years old. From the bubbles, scientists can measure directly how much carbon dioxide the air held long before anyone was there to record it, and the measurements show that the level today is higher than at any point in that whole period. The ice, in other words, is not a model of the past but a piece of it.

For years, publishers treated the audiobook as a small extra, produced for people who could not read print. It is now the fastest-growing part of the business, and in some countries it earns more than hardbacks do. Listeners are not, on the whole, people who have stopped reading; surveys find that they read as many printed books as anyone else and simply add listening to the hours they spend driving, cooking or walking. Whether listening counts as reading is a question that will not go away. Tests of comprehension find little difference for straightforward narrative, but readers of a difficult argument do better on paper, where they can stop, go back and see the shape of the page. Publishers have drawn their own conclusion: the two formats are now planned together, and many authors record their own books.

Modern concrete begins to crumble after fifty or sixty years in sea water. Roman harbour walls have stood in the Mediterranean for two thousand. For a long time the difference was put down to the volcanic ash that the Romans mixed into their concrete, and that is part of the answer. Recent work points to something the Romans may not have intended at all: small white lumps of lime left unmixed in the material. When a crack opens and water reaches one of these lumps, the lime dissolves and then sets again, filling the crack. What looked to earlier engineers like careless work now looks like the reason the walls are still there. Laboratories are already making concrete with lumps deliberately left in it.

Two thirds of the people in Europe cannot see the Milky Way from their homes. The glow that hides it comes mostly from lamps that send their light upwards, where nobody needs it. This is one of the few kinds of pollution that stops the moment the source is switched off, and a handful of towns have proved it. In them, street lamps have been fitted with shades, aimed downwards and dimmed after midnight; the stars came back within a single night, and the electricity bill fell. The argument that finally persuaded most councils, however, was not the sky at all. It was the growing evidence that bright light at night disturbs the sleep of the people living beneath it and confuses the insects and birds that navigate by the moon.

options.o5: copied the Roman recipe exactly as it was written

questions.why: 'Daha önceki mühendislere özensizlik gibi görünen şey' ifadesi, bir üstünlüğün kusur sanıldığını doğrudan söyler.
questions.trap_note: Yanlış bir yorumu hiç incelememiş olmakla karıştırır; parçaya göre mühendisler malzemeyi görmüş ama yanlış okumuştur.

questions.stem: The passage is mainly about ----.

options.o1: why Roman concrete outlasts the modern kind and what has been learned from it
options.o2: the history of harbour building around the Mediterranean
options.o3: the volcanic ash deposits that lie near the Bay of Naples
options.o4: the reasons why modern concrete is cheaper to produce
options.o5: the laboratories in which building materials are tested today

questions.why: Parça Roma betonunun neden daha uzun dayandığını açıklar ve bu bilginin bugün nasıl kullanıldığıyla kapanır.
questions.trap_note: Son cümledeki laboratuvarları konu sanır; oysa orası, açıklanan bulgunun sonucudur.

questions.stem: It can be inferred from the passage that light pollution differs from most other kinds because it ----.

options.o1: can be undone immediately once its cause is removed
options.o2: affects only the people who live in large cities
options.o3: has been measured accurately for over a century
options.o4: cannot be reduced without switching off all the lamps
options.o5: costs nothing at all to produce in the first place

questions.why: Parça bu kirliliğin kaynağı kapatıldığı anda sona erdiğini söyler; yıldızların tek gecede geri gelmesi bunu doğrular.
questions.trap_note: Çözümü tümüyle karanlığa çevirir; parçada lambalar söndürülmemiş, siperlik takılıp aşağı yöneltilmiştir.

questions.stem: According to the passage, the towns that changed their lighting ----.

options.o1: saw the stars return at once and paid less for electricity
options.o2: had to switch off their street lamps completely
options.o3: were the first places in Europe to use electric light
options.o4: found that the change cost more than they had expected
options.o5: made the change in order to protect birds and insects

questions.why: Parça sonucu iki maddede verir: yıldızlar tek gecede geri gelmiş ve elektrik faturası düşmüştür.
questions.trap_note: Kasabaların sonucunu belediyelerin gerekçesiyle karıştırır; hayvanlara ilişkin kanıt, kararı sonradan etkileyen argümandır.

questions.stem: It is clear from the passage that most councils were finally persuaded by ----.

options.o1: the effect of night light on people and on wildlife
options.o2: the wish to make the Milky Way visible again
options.o3: the pressure of astronomers living in the towns
options.o4: the cost of replacing the old street lamps
options.o5: a law that obliged them to fit shades to the lamps

questions.why: Parça belediyeleri ikna eden argümanın gökyüzü olmadığını açıkça söyler: uyku, kuşlar ve böcekler üzerindeki etkidir.
questions.trap_note: Parçanın açıkça dışladığı gerekçeyi seçer; 'gökyüzü hiç değildi' cümlesi göz ardı edilir.

questions.stem: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?

options.o1: Light pollution is easy to reverse, and health and wildlife proved the strongest arguments for doing so.
options.o2: The Milky Way has become invisible to almost everyone in Europe.
options.o3: Street lighting has become far too expensive for small towns.
options.o4: Insects and birds are disappearing from towns across the continent.
options.o5: Astronomers have been asking for darker skies for many years.

questions.why: Parça hem sorunun kolayca geri döndürülebilirliğini hem de belediyeleri ikna eden asıl gerekçeyi birlikte anlatır.
questions.trap_note: Açılış cümlesindeki istatistiği ana fikir sanır; o cümle sorunun boyutunu gösteren bir girişten ibarettir.

dialogue: Your class has started keeping a weather diary. Whose idea was that?
Ours. We wanted to know whether it really rains more here than it does in the next valley.
Not yet. We have only been measuring since March, so we cannot say anything for certain.

options.o1: And have you found out anything so far?
options.o2: Where exactly do you keep the rain gauge?
options.o3: How many of you take part in the measuring?
options.o4: Did anyone in the next valley agree to help you?
options.o5: Have you shown the diary to the other classes?

questions.why: 'Henüz değil. Mart'tan beri ölçüyoruz, kesin bir şey söyleyemeyiz' yanıtı, ancak bir sonuç elde edilip edilmediğini soran bir cümleyi karşılar.
questions.trap_note: Komşu vadiden söz ettiği için konuyla ilgilidir, ama 'henüz değil' yanıtının dayandığı ölçüm süresi açıklamasıyla bağ kurmaz.

dialogue: I would like to return this jacket. There is a hole in the lining.
I am sorry about that. Do you have the receipt with you?
That is not a problem. If you paid by card, we can find the purchase in the system.

options.o1: I am afraid I threw it away, but I paid with my card.
options.o2: Yes, here it is, together with the guarantee card.
options.o3: I bought the jacket as a present for my brother.
options.o4: Could I exchange it for the same one in blue?
options.o5: The hole was already there when I opened the package.

questions.why: 'Sorun değil. Kartla ödediyseniz alışverişi sistemde bulabiliriz' yanıtı, ancak fişin bulunmadığı ama kartla ödendiği bilgisinden sonra anlamlıdır.
questions.trap_note: Sorulan soruyu doğrudan yanıtlar ama olumlu yanıt verir; fiş elde olduğunda 'sorun değil' demenin ve sistemde arama yapmanın bir gerekçesi kalmaz.

dialogue: You have translated the same novel twice, thirty years apart. Why go back to it?
Because the language I used in 1990 now sounds like 1990 rather than like the book.
No, the original has not changed at all. What has changed is the Turkish that a reader expects to find on the page.

options.o1: Do you mean that a new edition of the original had appeared in the meantime?
options.o2: How long did the second translation take you to finish?
options.o3: Which of the two versions do you prefer yourself?
options.o4: Did you work from the same dictionary on both occasions?
options.o5: Have other translators criticised your first version?

questions.why: 'Hayır, özgün metin hiç değişmedi' yanıtı, ancak özgün metnin değişip değişmediğini soran bir cümleyi karşılayabilir.
questions.trap_note: Konuyla ilgili doğal bir sorudur ama 'hayır' ile yanıtlanamaz; çevirmenin verdiği yanıt bir tercih değil, bir düzeltmedir.

dialogue: The wall you are looking at was built without mortar, and it has stood for four hundred years.
Exactly. Each stone was shaped until it fitted the ones around it, and the weight does the rest.

options.o1: So the stones are held in place by their own shape and weight?
options.o2: Was the wall built by the villagers themselves?
options.o3: How high was the wall when it was first finished?
options.o4: Does anybody still build walls in this way today?
options.o5: Has the wall ever been repaired since it was built?

questions.why: Rehberin 'Aynen öyle' diyerek taşların biçimlendirilmesini ve ağırlığın işi tamamlamasını anlatması, ancak bunu tahmin eden bir cümleden sonra gelebilir.
questions.trap_note: Duvar örme tekniğiyle ilgilidir ama bir tahmin içermez; 'Aynen öyle' onayını karşılayacak bir önerme sunmaz.

dialogue: I have been taking the tablets for ten days and the cough is no better.
Twice a day, with breakfast and with dinner, exactly as it says on the box.

options.o1: How often have you been taking them, and at what times?
options.o2: Have you ever had a cough like this one before?
options.o3: Are you taking any other medicine at the same time?
options.o4: Does the cough get worse during the night?
options.o5: Did the pharmacist explain the side effects to you?

questions.why: 'Günde iki kez, kahvaltıda ve akşam yemeğinde' yanıtı, yalnızca ilacın ne sıklıkta ve ne zaman alındığını soran bir cümleyi karşılar.
questions.trap_note: İlaçla ilgili makul bir sorudur, ancak yanıt başka bir ilacı değil, aynı ilacın alınma düzenini anlatır.

questions.stem: It is not the noise that keeps me awake but the light from the street.

options.o1: What stops me from sleeping is the street light rather than the noise.
options.o2: Neither the noise nor the light from the street keeps me awake.
options.o3: The noise keeps me awake more than the light from the street does.
options.o4: I would sleep better if there were no noise in the street.
options.o5: The light from the street is just as disturbing as the noise.

questions.why: It is not X but Y kalıbı iki etken arasında seçim yapar: uyutmayan gürültü değil, sokak lambasının ışığıdır.
questions.trap_note: Seçimi eşitliğe çevirir; biri elenirken diğeri öne çıkarılmışken, iki etken aynı düzeye getirilir.

questions.stem: The library will stay open during the holiday, though with shorter hours.

options.o1: The library is not closing for the holiday, but it will be open for fewer hours than usual.
options.o2: The library will close during the holiday and reopen later with shorter hours.
options.o3: The library keeps the same hours whether it is a holiday or not.
options.o4: The library has to shorten its hours in order to stay open at all.
options.o5: During the holiday the library will be open for longer than usual.

questions.why: Cümlenin iki yarısı korunmalıdır: kütüphane tatilde açıktır, ancak çalışma saatleri kısalmıştır.
questions.trap_note: İki bilgiyi bir koşul ilişkisine sokar; 'saatler kısa olsa da açık' ifadesi, 'açık kalabilmesi için kısaltmak zorunda' anlamına çevrilir.

questions.stem: Little did the organisers know that half the audience would arrive an hour early.

options.o1: The organisers had no idea that half the audience would turn up an hour before time.
options.o2: The organisers knew a little about the audience arriving an hour early.
options.o3: The organisers told half the audience to arrive an hour early.
options.o4: Half the audience knew that the organisers would be an hour late.
options.o5: The organisers expected only half the audience to arrive on time.

questions.why: Little did ... know devrik kalıbı 'hiç bilmiyorlardı' anlamı taşır; buradaki little olumsuzdur.
questions.trap_note: little'ı 'biraz' diye okur; olumsuz bir niceleyici, kısmi bir bilgiye dönüşünce cümlenin anlamı tersine döner.

questions.stem: Whatever the weather, the market is held in the square every Tuesday.

options.o1: The market takes place in the square on Tuesdays regardless of the weather.
options.o2: The market is held in the square on Tuesdays only when the weather is good.
options.o3: Bad weather may force the market to move out of the square on a Tuesday.
options.o4: Whenever the weather is bad, the Tuesday market is cancelled.
options.o5: The square is used for the market on any day when the weather allows it.

questions.why: Whatever the weather kalıbı havanın hiçbir etkisi olmadığını bildirir; pazar her salı aynı yerde kurulur.
questions.trap_note: Havayı bir koşula dönüştürür; koşulsuz bir düzen, havanın izin verdiği günlere bağlanmış olur.

questions.stem: ---- A dog can be trained to lie down when it smells one particular chemical, and researchers have used this to test breath, urine and even worn clothing. Results in the laboratory have been remarkable; results in hospitals have been mixed, because a dog that works for eight hours grows bored long before a machine would.

options.o1: The nose of a dog is being tried out as a medical instrument.
options.o2: Dogs have lived alongside human beings for many thousands of years.
options.o3: Hospitals are among the most expensive buildings to run.
options.o4: Machines are now able to detect almost any chemical in the air.
options.o5: Training a dog takes patience and a great deal of time.

questions.why: Boşluk paragrafın ilk cümlesidir ve hem konuyu hem de sonraki cümledeki köpek eğitiminin amacını tanıtmak zorundadır.
questions.trap_note: Köpek eğitiminden söz ettiği için doğru görünür, ama paragrafın konusu eğitimin zorluğu değil, koku alma duyusunun tıpta kullanılmasıdır.

questions.stem: The Sahara has not always been a desert. Cave paintings deep inside it show swimmers, cattle and rivers full of fish. ---- The change was not caused by anything that people did; it came from a slow wobble in the tilt of the earth, which moved the rain belt south. The same wobble will one day bring the rain back.

options.o1: Six thousand years ago the region was green, and it dried out within a few centuries.
options.o2: Similarly, the Arabian peninsula was once covered by forest.
options.o3: These paintings were first photographed in the 1930s.
options.o4: Cattle are still kept along the southern edge of the desert.
options.o5: Therefore, the desert is likely to grow larger every year.

questions.why: Boşluktan sonraki cümle 'the change' diyerek bir değişime gönderme yapar; bu değişimin ne zaman ve nasıl olduğu boşlukta verilmelidir.
questions.trap_note: Bir önceki cümlede geçen paintings sözcüğüne tutunur, ama sonraki cümledeki 'the change' ifadesine karşılık gelecek bir değişim tanıtmaz.

questions.stem: A lock on a canal looks like a simple thing: two gates and a chamber between them. ---- Each time a boat goes through, a chamber full of water runs downhill and is lost to the river below. On a busy canal that can be millions of litres a day, which is why many locks now have side ponds that catch part of the water and give it back to the next boat.

options.o1: The cost of using one, however, is measured in water.
options.o2: Therefore, canals are cheaper to build than railways are.
options.o3: Moreover, the gates are usually opened by hand.
options.o4: These boats are rarely longer than twenty metres.
options.o5: This chamber was invented in China more than a thousand years ago.

questions.why: Paragraf basitlik izleniminden gizli bir maliyete geçer; boşluk bu dönüşü kuran however cümlesidir.
questions.trap_note: Bir önceki cümlede geçen chamber sözcüğüne gönderme yapar, ama paragrafı su kaybı konusuna değil tarihe çevirir.

questions.stem: For two hundred years the recipe for Prussian blue was a trade secret, and painters paid for it accordingly. Then a chemist published it in a journal, and within five years the price had fallen by nine tenths. ---- It appears in the sky of half the paintings of the period, in printed wallpaper and, eventually, on the paper used for engineering drawings. A secret had become a background.

options.o1: That collapse in price changed what the colour was used for.
options.o2: Such journals were read by very few people at the time.
options.o3: The chemist himself never received any payment for it.
options.o4: Painters, however, went on mixing their own colours.
options.o5: This wallpaper was printed in only three colours.

questions.why: Boşluktan sonra rengin nerelerde kullanıldığı sıralanır; boşluk, fiyat düşüşünü bu yayılmaya bağlayan cümledir.
questions.trap_note: Bir önceki cümledeki kimyacıya gönderme yapar, ama sonraki cümledeki kullanım listesini hazırlayacak bir bağ kurmaz.

sentences: The Dutch city of Utrecht has built a car park for twelve thousand bicycles under its main station.
The Netherlands exports more flowers than any other country in the world.
A screen at the entrance shows which rows still have space, so that nobody rides up and down looking for a place.
The first twenty-four hours are free, which keeps the racks moving instead of letting them fill up with abandoned bikes.
Three quarters of the people who arrive by bicycle leave the station on foot or by train.
questions.why: II. cümle çiçek ihracatına ilişkin genel bir bilgidir; paragrafın anlattığı bisiklet otoparkıyla hiçbir bağı yoktur.
questions.trap_note: V. cümle otoparkın kendisinden söz etmediği için kopuk sanılır; oysa otoparkın istasyonla nasıl birlikte çalıştığını göstererek paragrafı tamamlar.

sentences: Garum, a sauce made from fermented fish, flavoured almost every dish on a Roman table.
It was produced in coastal factories, where fish and salt were left in stone tanks for months.
Amphorae stamped with the name of the maker have been dug up from Britain to the Black Sea.
Roman roads were built in straight lines wherever the ground allowed it.
Cooks today describe the taste as close to the fish sauces that are still made in Southeast Asia.
questions.why: IV. cümle yol yapımına geçer; paragrafın konusu olan balık sosunun üretimi ve yayılımıyla ilgisi yoktur.
questions.trap_note: V. cümle bugüne atladığı için dışarıdan eklenmiş gibi durur; oysa sosun tadını tarif ederek paragrafı bitirir.

sentences: The tuatara of New Zealand looks like a lizard but belongs to an order of reptiles that is otherwise extinct.
Its ancestors were already old when the first dinosaurs appeared.
New Zealand is made up of two large islands and a great many smaller ones.
It grows so slowly that it may not breed until it is twenty years old, and it can live past a hundred.
Rats brought by ships wiped it out on the mainland, and it survives on islands where the rats have been removed.
questions.why: III. cümle ülkenin coğrafyasını anlatır; paragrafın konusu olan hayvanın özellikleri ve durumuyla bağ kurmaz.
questions.trap_note: II. cümle çok uzak bir geçmişe gittiği için kopuk sanılır; oysa türün ne kadar eski olduğunu göstererek ilk cümleyi destekler.

sentences: Before refrigeration, ice was cut from frozen lakes in winter and sold in summer.
Traders packed the blocks in sawdust, which kept them frozen for months.
Ships carried ice from New England as far as Calcutta, and about two thirds of each cargo arrived.
Calcutta is built on the delta of the Ganges.
The trade collapsed within a generation, once machines could make ice anywhere.
questions.why: IV. cümle bir şehrin coğrafi konumunu verir; buz ticaretinin nasıl yürüdüğünü anlatan akışa hiçbir şey katmaz.
questions.trap_note: III. cümledeki kayıp oranı konudan sapıyormuş gibi görünür; oysa ticaretin ne kadar zor koşullarda yürüdüğünü gösterir.

sentences: A hummingbird has to eat almost its own weight in nectar every day.
To survive the night, it lowers its body temperature and slows its heart until it is almost cold.
In this state, which is called torpor, it uses a fraction of the energy it would otherwise need.
Warming up again in the morning can take twenty minutes, and the bird cannot fly until it has finished.
Nectar is produced by flowers in order to attract insects as well as birds.
questions.why: V. cümle çiçeklerin nektar üretme amacına geçer; paragrafın anlattığı gece hayatta kalma düzeneğini ilerletmez.
questions.trap_note: IV. cümle sabaha geçtiği için konudan kopuk sanılır; oysa torpor durumunun bedelini anlatarak paragrafı tamamlar.

vocabulary: uyuşukluk hâli, kış uykusuna benzer durum
